basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Models an early or loosely bounded effort with a case for change, before or without becoming a project or programme.
Formalisation into a project or programme creates a new master with typed derivation, not a rename.
Holds options and hypotheses about value as explicit assertions to be tested.
Links work it coordinates without owning those work items.

may: Draft a case for change from cited problem evidence.
Appraise options against stated criteria for review.
Link related work and report dependencies.
Track gate dates and hypothesis results.
mustNot: Treat an initiative as an approved project with budget authority.
Present hypotheses or options as validated results.
Commit resources or budget without mandate.
Take over ownership of linked work items.
Drop stakeholder concerns from the record.
requiresHuman: Approving the mandate, sponsorship and guardrails.
Formalising, transferring or stopping the initiative.

considerations: Early initiatives can affect people before formal impact assessment; stakeholder concerns should be captured early.
Experiments within initiatives that involve people need consent and oversight.

items: An initiative has a name, a sponsor, a problem or opportunity statement, a mandate and a status.
It is confused with a project, programme, campaign, strategic objective or idea backlog item.
Untracked spending on initiatives that never got a mandate.
Duplicated efforts when overlapping initiatives are not linked.
The Open Group ArchiMate 3.2 work package and course of action elements.
